text: The Patriots limp into Week 4 facing the Bills at Highmark Stadium on Sunday, October 4 at 1 PM ET, and the trajectory couldn't be more alarming—New England sits dead last in the NFL with just 9.7 offensive points per game, a stunning underperformance that has become impossible to ignore after Drake Maye's two-interception, one-fumble disaster in a 35-6 demolition by the Jaguars' Lawrence, who threw three touchdown passes in what amounted to a complete offensive meltdown. The quarterback himself acknowledged the situation is "unacceptable," calling out both his own play and the offense's supporting cast, while beat writers are openly questioning whether the Patriots are even using Maye correctly in the first place. Adding insult to injury, the infrastructure around the young signal-caller took another shot Tuesday when guard Greg Van Roten landed on injured reserve with a thigh injury, forcing the team to release linebacker Riley Wilson from the practice squad in a pair of moves that underscore just how dire the roster situation has become.
